_comment: Fabrication design rules for the Courant Rev A board, as a KiCad project
file. scripts/route.py writes this next to dist/courant.kicad_pcb so that
the router, the DRC and the Gerber export all read the same numbers.
Why these values, and not KiCad's defaults (0.2 mm track / 0.2 mm clearance
/ 0.6 mm via): the XC7A35T's FTG256 balls are 0.5 mm pads on a 1.0 mm
pitch, so the gap between two neighbouring balls is 0.5 mm. Escaping a
signal between them needs width + 2 x clearance to fit in that gap, and
KiCad's defaults need 0.6 mm. At 0.15/0.15 it is 0.45 mm and it fits.
The same argument sets the via: a dog-bone via sits in the diagonal gap
between four balls, 0.707 mm from each ball centre. With a 0.55 mm via pad
and a 0.5 mm ball pad that leaves 0.707 - 0.25 - 0.275 = 0.182 mm, which
clears 0.15 mm. A 0.6 mm via would leave 0.157 mm and would not.
0.25 mm drill in a 1.6 mm board is a 6.4:1 aspect ratio (<= 8:1 preferred)
and the 0.15 mm annular ring is past the 0.13 mm knee where breakout risk
collapses. All of this is inside every standard 6-layer process.
The Power class widens the rails. It keeps the Default clearance and via,
deliberately: VCCO, VCCINT and VCCAUX balls are inside the same 1.0 mm ball
field as the signals, so a wider power via could not be fanned out at all.

GND has its own class so the router can be told where signals may go without also telling GND where it may not. scripts/route.py restricts every class except Ground to the non-plane layers via a Specctra `use_layer` clause. The earlier attempt marked the plane layers `(type power)` instead, which does not mean 'no signals here' -- it makes the layer unavailable for connections at all, so GND pins could not reach their own plane. That single mistake left 50-odd GND connections unrouted in three separate routing runs and was misread as the board being too dense.
